description:
Problem: oracle findings arrive only after a PR exists. Each NO-SHIP or SHIP WITH FIXES costs a new head and another full CI and oracle round of 2h or more at 2026-10-25 load; #3465 and #3472 each lost a round to a High finding that day, and authoring agents skipped the pre-publication self-review. A local review cannot count towards oracle-gate, because the author controls what is reviewed; it can catch findings before the PR exists.

Outcome (owner decisions 2026-10-25): make pr-open runs a local oracle review of the branch's diff against the merge base with origin/develop before it pushes or opens anything.
- Same machinery as CI: a local plan built from git (cli.py plan gains a local mode: base and head SHAs, no PR number, no prior reviews), the same TypeSafe classification, policy, reviewer selection, templates, harness and redaction, and the attempt-loop command from oracle-verdict-single-job-20261025. No second loop.
- Classifier key: TYPESAFE_API_KEY from the macOS keychain service TYPESAFE_API_KEY. When it is absent (including cloud sessions), use the fixed default: the policy's medium-bucket reviewer with the standard template, or the gate template when review-machinery files change, and print that the default was used.
- Credentials: local sessions use the oracle-local gateway client at http://127.0.0.1:4000 with ~/.omp/oracle-gateway/local-client.token; cloud builders use the oracle-cloud client over the tailnet from their environment (oracle-gateway-cloud-builder-access-20261025).
- Blocking: Critical or High findings make pr-open refuse. A PR body line `Local oracle override: <non-empty reason>` lets the author proceed on a false positive; pr-open keeps the line in the body so the reason is visible on the PR.
- Failure mode: block until it can run. Gateway unreachable, timeout, quota exhaustion or reviewer absence makes pr-open refuse with the reason; the override line does not cover this case.
- Scope: it reviews the committed HEAD that pr-open will push, never uncommitted changes. A result is cached by patch digest, policy hash and harness version, so re-running pr-open on an unchanged patch reuses it instead of reviewing again.
- Output is labelled as a local advisory review that may differ from the CI oracle. It posts nothing to GitHub.

Decision gates:
1. Before editing, confirm that the attempt-loop command from oracle-verdict-single-job-20261025 can run without GitHub event inputs. If it cannot, extend it minimally in this item; never add a second loop.
2. Reverts are unaffected: make trunk-revert opens its PR with gh pr create directly (scripts/trunk_revert.py:339-356, Makefile trunk-revert target), not through make pr-open. Re-check before editing; if that has changed, stop and ask whether develop-recovery reverts skip the local review.
4. Harness version: the local review runs only when the installed omp matches the version CI's reviewers use (the pin in .github/workflows/oracle-verdict.yml); otherwise it cannot run and pr-open refuses with the version mismatch, under the block-until-it-can-run decision.
3. Concurrency: at most one local review at a time per machine (a file lock), because local reviews share gateway accounts and quota with CI reviews. If measured waits make pr-open impractical, record the numbers and ask the owner before raising the limit.

Item guardrails: no change to the CI oracle, oracle-gate, the policy or selection logic; the local result never counts as a verdict and is never posted; no token or key is printed or written to the repository; pushes after the PR exists are out of scope (they get the CI oracle). This item supersedes, for its own scope only, the 'no ship-no-ship/local-executor work' exclusion recorded in the plan of oracle-response-live-verification-20261021 (owner decision 2026-10-25).
Owner one-time step (UX): store the TypeSafe key with `security add-generic-password -s TYPESAFE_API_KEY -a "$USER" -w`; until then the fixed default applies. Document it.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. Never use git stash (refs/stash is shared across worktrees). Commit as Joe Harris <joeharris76@gmail.com>, staging explicit paths only; no git add -A, no --no-verify, no SKIP, no agent trailers. Durable text (commits, PR bodies, docs, comments) carries no tracker ids, session labels or plan references. Maintained code has no explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check). Run make docs-reference-inventory-check and make doc-contracts-guard in addition to make pr-preflight. Close out with make pr-open, oracle SHIP on the exact head, make pr-arm; never raw gh pr merge, never a stand-in or bypass on these oracle soundness paths.
